question: In Figure 9E-12, what minimum distance separates the advance motor-vehicle stop line from the intersection stop line across the bicycle box?
model_answer: Direct Answer: The minimum distance is 10 feet. Figure 9E-12 annotates the dimension between the advance stop line (where motor vehicles stop) and the intersection stop line as "10 ft MIN.," reflecting the Standard that the bicycle box depth between those edges shall be at least 10 feet. Standards (mandatory): - "If used, the distance from the upstream edge of the bicycle box that is nearest to the stop line for motor vehicles to the downstream edge of the bicycle box that is nearest the crosswalk or intersection shall be at least 10 feet. At least one bicycle symbol marking (see Figure 9E-12) shall be used in the bicycle box." Options (permitted): - A bicycle box may be used to increase the visibility of stopped bicycles on the approach to a signalized intersection during the red signal indication displayed to motor vehicles behind the box. - Green-colored pavement may be used in a bicycle box. Visual evidence: - [Image 1] Figure 9E-12 (Sheet 1 of 2) shows the bicycle box across one lane with a "10 ft MIN." dimension between the intersection stop line and the advance stop line. - [Image 2] The full-page view of Sheet 1 of Figure 9E-12 confirms the "10 ft MIN." dimension separating the intersection stop line from the advance stop line. - [Image 3] Sheet 2 of Figure 9E-12 (bicycle box across multiple lanes) also shows a "10 ft MIN." dimension for the bicycle box depth, along with the R10-6a STOP HERE ON RED sign and R3-7bP EXCEPT BICYCLES plaque. - [Image 4] Page 1105 shows the Section 9E.12 Standard text requiring the at-least-10-foot distance between the bicycle box edges. Citations: - Section 9E.12 Standard §6 (p.1105) - Section 9E.12 Option §1 (p.1105) - Section 9E.12 Option §12 (p.1106) - Figure 9E-12 (p.1106)
